arxiv-2204-01596.title: Time-Frequency Analysis Lecture Notes
arxiv-2204-01596.creator: Markus Faulhuber
arxiv-2204-01596.description: Abstract These lecture notes accompanied the course Time-Frequency Analysis given at the Faculty of Mathematics of the University of Vienna in the summer term 2021. The material is suitable for an advanced undergraduate course in mathematics or a mathematics class for PhD students. Besides standard linear algebra and calculus only some basics from functional analysis are needed.

arxiv-2204-09105.title: An improved central limit theorem and fast convergence rates for entropic transportation costs
arxiv-2204-09105.creator: Eustasio del Barrio, Alberto González-Sanz, Jean-Michel Loubes, Jonathan Niles-Weed
arxiv-2204-09105.description: Abstract We prove a central limit theorem for the entropic transportation cost between subgaussian probability measures, centered at the population cost. This is the first result which allows for asymptotically valid inference for entropic optimal transport between measures which are not necessarily discrete.

arxiv-2212-05715.title: Integrated optimization of train timetables rescheduling and response vehicles on a disrupted metro line
arxiv-2212-05715.creator: Hui Wang, Jialin Liu, Feng Li, Hao Ji, Bin Jia, Ziyou Gao
arxiv-2212-05715.description: Abstract When an unexpected metro disruption occurs, metro managers need to reschedule timetables to avoid trains going into the disruption area, and transport passengers stranded at disruption stations as quickly as possible. This paper proposes a two-stage optimization model to jointly make decisions for two tasks.

arxiv-2212-14223.title: Global quantum phase diagram and non-Abelian chiral spin liquid in a spin-3/2 square lattice antiferromagnet

arxiv-2212-14223.description: Abstract Since strong quantum fluctuations are essential for the emergence of quantum spin liquids, there have been extensive exploration and identification of spin liquid candidates in spin- 1 / 2 1/2 systems, while such activities are rare in higher spin systems.

arxiv-2305-05130.creator: submitted in partial
arxiv-2305-05130.description: Abstract ABSTRACT Zero Distribution of Generated Taylor Polynomials Our goal in this paper is to study the zero distribution of a sequence of polynomials whose coefficients satisfy a three-term recurrence. Equivalently, these polynomials are Taylor polynomials of a rational function with a polynomial denominator of degree 2.

arxiv-2305-15878.title: LFTK: Handcrafted Features in Computational Linguistics
arxiv-2305-15878.creator: Bruce W. Lee, Jason Hyung-Jong Lee
arxiv-2305-15878.description: Abstract Past research has identified a rich set of handcrafted linguistic features that can potentially assist various tasks. However, their extensive number makes it difficult to effectively select and utilize existing handcrafted features. Coupled with the problem of inconsistent implementation across research works, there has been no categorization scheme or generally-accepted feature names. This creates unwanted confusion.

arxiv-2406-02001.title: Higher-order Common Information
arxiv-2406-02001.creator: Jan Østergaard
arxiv-2406-02001.description: Abstract Shannon mutual information quantifies dependence between two random variables. We introduce higher-order common information (HCI), a measure of statistical relevance across n n random variables. The HCI constructs a sequence of stochastically degraded representations. At each stage, the representation maximizes the amount of relevant information to the next source under a limited information budget.

arxiv-2409-08949.title: Generic and ML Workloads in an HPC Datacenter: Node Energy, Job Failures, and Node-Job Analysis Thanks: *Equal contributions, joint first authors.
arxiv-2409-08949.creator: Xiaoyu Chu ∗1 , Daniel Hofstätter ∗2 , Shashikant Ilager 2 , Sacheendra Talluri 1 , Duncan Kampert 3 , Damian Podareanu 3 , Dmitry Duplyakin 4 , Ivona Brandic 2 , Alexandru Iosup 1
arxiv-2409-08949.description: Abstract HPC datacenters offer a backbone to the modern digital society. Increasingly, they run Machine Learning (ML) jobs next to generic, compute-intensive workloads, supporting science, business, and other decision-making processes. However, understanding how ML jobs impact the operation of HPC datacenters, relative to generic jobs, remains desirable but understudied.

arxiv-2410-12049.title: Sabiá-3 Technical Report
arxiv-2410-12049.creator: Hugo Abonizio, Thales Sales Almeida, Thiago Laitz
arxiv-2410-12049.description: Abstract This report presents Sabiá-3, our new flagship language model, and Sabiazinho-3, a more cost-effective sibling. The models were trained on a large brazilian-centric corpus. Evaluations across diverse professional and academic benchmarks show a strong performance on Portuguese and Brazil-related tasks. Sabiá-3 shows large improvements in comparison to our previous best of model, Sabia-2 Medium, especially in reasoning-intensive tasks.

arxiv-2412-10096.title: Reward Machine Inference for Robotic Manipulation
arxiv-2412-10096.creator: Mattijs Baert, Sam Leroux, Pieter Simoens
arxiv-2412-10096.description: Abstract Learning from Demonstrations (LfD) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) have enabled robot agents to accomplish complex tasks. Reward Machines (RMs) enhance RL’s capability to train policies over extended time horizons by structuring high-level task information. In this work, we introduce a novel LfD approach for learning RMs directly from visual demonstrations of robotic manipulation tasks.

pmc-11397856.title: The Influence of Oil and Thermal Aging on the Sealing Characteristics of NBR Seals
pmc-11397856.creator: Yiding Li, Jian Wu, Zhihao Chen, Ziqi Zhang, Benlong Su, Youshan Wang, Changwoon Nah
pmc-11397856.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Nitrile Butadiene Rubber (NBR) is widely used as a sealing material due to its excellent mechanical properties and good oil resistance. However, when using NBR material, the seal structure is unable to avoid the negative effects of rubber aging. Hence, the influence of oil and thermal aging on the characteristics of NBR seals was studied by coupling the mechanical behavioral changes with the tribological behavioral changes of NBR in oil and the thermal environment.

pmc-12427974.title: miR-451 Is a Driver of Lipotoxic Injury in Patients with Diabetic Cardiomyopathy
pmc-12427974.creator: Sarah Costantino, Shafeeq A Mohammed, Federico Ranocchi, Francesco Zito, Valentina Delfine, Nazha Hamdani, Maria Cristina Vinci, Giovanni Melina, Francesco Paneni, Roger Schneiter, Museer Ahmad Lone
pmc-12427974.description: MicroRNA 451 (miR-451) is emerging as a pivotal mediator of cardiac damage in experimental models of diabetic cardiomyopathy. Whether miR-451 plays a detrimental role in the human diabetic myocardium is unknown. The present study investigates miR-451’s role in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D).

pmc-12822344.title: Molecular determinants of lung function decline: a multi-level analysis of gene expression
pmc-12822344.creator: Zaid W. Elhusseini, Omar Rafique, Min Hyung Ryu, Peter Castaldi, Don D. Sin, Ingo Ruczinski, Craig P. Hersh
pmc-12822344.description: BackgroundChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by progressive lung function decline, commonly measured by forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1). Uncovering the genetic basis of FEV1 decline is essential for understanding COPD pathophysiology and for developing therapies. We hypothesized that gene expression patterns in inflammatory pathways are associated with FEV1 decline.

pmc-13100276.title: Longitudinal Evolution of Phenotypes in Severe Asthma: Clinical Implications for Personalized Medicine
pmc-13100276.creator: Francisco Javier Álvarez-Gutiérrez, Marina Blanco Aparicio, José Valverde Molina
pmc-13100276.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). cross-sectional, limiting understanding of asthma's dynamic nature over time. Various recent studies support abandoning a static view of asthma and considering it an evolutionary process, characterized by transitions and overlaps in phenotypes throughout the patient's life.1 In this regard, recent views consistently emphasize that phenotypes associated with type 2, non-type 2, and mixed inflammation are not mutually exclusive entities, but rather coexist and interrelate in response to environmental and infectious factors, comorbidities, and the plasticity of the immune system.

pmc-13531287.title: Outcomes of transition from selexipag to parenteral prostacyclin analogues in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension
pmc-13531287.creator: Ebrahim AlEissa, Lisa Kolkman, Ali Kapasi, Defen Peng, Steeve Provencher, Nathan Brunner, John Swiston
pmc-13531287.description: ExtractPulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) remains a progressive, incurable condition often associated with poor outcomes despite advances in therapy [1]. Selexipag, an oral selective prostacyclin receptor agonist, is associated with reduced hospitalisations and slower disease progression when added to an endothelin receptor antagonist (ERA) and/or a phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitor (PDE5i) in patients with PAH [2].
